chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man marries off his male slave to his female slave, he separates them if he wishes."

I asked him about a man who marries his female slave to a free man or a slave belonging to other people; is he entitled to take her back from him? He said: 'No, unless he sells her. And if he sells her, and the one who bought her wishes to separate them, he separates them.'

key_terms.يَنْزِعَهَا: to take her back / withdraw her

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a master separating the marriage of his slaves or selling a married female slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the master's prerogative (*ikhtiyar*) to dissolve the marital bond of his slaves, distinguishing between retaining ownership versus transferring it through sale. It establishes that while a master cannot unilaterally reclaim a female slave married to another party without selling her, the new owner inherits the right to separate the couple, reflecting the fluidity of slave marriages in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the legal principle that the master's ownership of the slave supersedes the stability of the marital contract, a key concept in *Fiqh al-Imamiyyah* regarding *milk al-yamin*.
